effect: The completed picture shows separate cells wrapping sections of one continuous nerve extension, with gaps where channels are exposed. It also says the insulation helps messages travel quickly.
reaction: The cross-section made it clearer which membrane belongs to which cell, though I still don't understand exactly how the gaps speed up messages.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the channels was most worthwhile: it explained that a message moves through local electrical changes rather than one ion traveling the whole length.

leastWorthwhile.text: Developing the insulating cells felt more like following the only offered pairing than making a meaningful choice, although the cross-section helped explain their shape.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the long extension remains part of one cell while other cells wrap separate lengths of it.

arbitrary.text: No action seemed purposeless, but the development messengers were named pairings rather than choices I could independently work out in detail.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see where nerve messages go next. The channel explanation and the finished wrapped fibre made me curious, even though several choices were straightforward.
